subject: SIGMA: Dedicated pool saturation - immediate mitigation & exec summary
messages:
From: Darren Cole <ops@sigma-finance.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike: 95th pct latency + errors, reserved throughput not met

Naomi,

We started seeing a sustained latency spike and increased error rates in our prod inference path beginning ~08:50 PDT. 95th percentile token latency has jumped from ~180ms to ~980ms, and error rate on generation calls is ~4.1% (baseline <0.2%). Throughput is visibly below our contracted reserved capacity — requests queue at the edge and are timing out. This is impacting live risk-scoring (SLA 99.9% p99) and causing automated fallbacks in our stack.

We have screenshots of retries and a list of affected request IDs (attached) — can you confirm whether this is a configuration/regression on your side or a temporary saturation event? We need an ETA on mitigation and whether you can move traffic to an alternate capacity tier. If this is an SRE/ops issue, please escalate to the team that manages Dedicated pools.

This is high severity for us; our CISO (Leah Torres) is on this thread. Please advise next steps.

Thanks,
Darren
Operations
Sigma Finance
[attachment: sigma_request_ids_20270405.txt]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Spike: 95th pct latency + errors, reserved throughput not met

Forwarding Sigma ops alert — production latency and errors, they report reserved throughput not being honored. Initial ask: immediate mitigation + ETA.

Quick triage notes (observed while I pulled logs):
- Customer's dedicated pool shows sustained enqueue times and queue growth starting ~08:45 PDT.
- Error signatures indicate token-generation timeouts and occasional OOM/CONTEXT_EVICT in runtime logs.
- Attached: diagnostic dump requested from their side and a short metrics CSV we pulled.

Requesting immediate actions:
1) Rishi: can you confirm whether this is kernel-level contention or a scheduling regression (recent autoscaler/placement change rolled last week)?
2) Vivek/Marissa: please advise on policy to burst this customer to the shared burst tier while we investigate; customer expects traffic to be moved ASAP to avoid production impacts.
3) Markus: exec awareness — this is Sigma (large financial customer). They will expect an ETA + remediation plan to their CISO.

I'll prepare a short external note once we have options.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:58:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike: 95th pct latency + errors, reserved throughput not met

Naomi / team,

Quick technical readout from runtime diagnostics I pulled from the pool (mirrored logs attached):
- Observed KV cache churn leading to repeated key evictions; this aligns with token latency increases as KV misses cause repeated decoding cost.
- One of the nodes in Sigma's pool is reporting repeated GPU driver resets ~08:50-09:05 (NVIDIA TDR-like events). That node's instances show a drop in available batch slots.
- Scheduler backlog indicates requests are being queued rather than routed to other warm nodes — autoscaler did not trigger additional allocation within the 5m window.

Immediate steps I can run now (15-30 min):
A) Mark the problem node as out-of-service and rebalance traffic across remaining nodes. This will reduce available capacity slightly but remove the driver-reset instability.
B) Force a proactive warm-up of 2 additional burst instances from shared capacity to handle incoming load. This requires ops approval (billing/contract override).
C) Enable temporary KV cache relaxation (reduce strictness of eviction threshold) to reduce churn — low-risk for correctness but may increase memory pressure.

If we do A + B we should see queue reduction and 95th pct latency drop within ~20 minutes. Recommendation: proceed with A immediately, B if customer agrees to burst or if we can approve within 10 minutes.

Attaching: runtime_logs_excerpt_20270405.txt, pool_node_status_20270405.csv

—Rishi
Senior Applied Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike: 95th pct latency + errors, reserved throughput not met

Do A immediately. Approve B for up to 2x baseline burst for the next 3 hours to stabilize — authorize billing team to apply customer goodwill credit if needed.

Marissa: please coordinate the customer-facing communication and confirm with Procurement/Finance on credit. Markus: FYI for executive exposure.

I'll draft an exec summary for Sigma's CISO once we have post-mitigation metrics.

Vivek
Head of Customer Reliability

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Darren Cole <ops@sigma-finance.com>, Leah Torres <leah.torres@sigma-finance.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 10:25:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Spike: 95th pct latency + errors, reserved throughput not met

Darren / Leah — quick update and immediate mitigation plan: 

What happened (short):
- One node in your dedicated pool experienced repeated GPU driver resets, which reduced available batch slots and caused scheduler queuing. Simultaneously we observed KV cache churn increasing decode cost.

What we did (now):
- Removed the unstable node from the pool and rebalanced traffic (Rishi).
- Brought 2 warm burst instances online from shared capacity to absorb immediate load (approved internally).
- Applied a temporary KV-cache relaxation to reduce eviction churn.

What you should see:
- Expect 95th pct latency to return close to baseline within ~20 minutes and error rate to fall to <0.3% as queues drain.
- We will monitor for the next 3 hours and keep you updated every 30 minutes.

Next steps we are taking:
- Full post-mortem and remediation plan (hardware replacement, driver rollback, scheduler tweak) within 48 hours.
- If any residual customer impact remains after mitigation we will provide a usage credit consistent with your contract; Marissa will coordinate specifics with Procurement.

Attachments: diagnostic_dump_20270405.zip, pool_metrics_qs_20270405.csv

Apologies for the disruption — we know this is high-impact and are treating it as high priority. I will send a concise executive summary to Leah and your leadership once we confirm stabilization.

—Naomi
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIGMA: Dedicated pool saturation - immediate mitigation & exec summary

Closing notes / follow-up actions for internal tracker:
- Customer saw stabilization at ~10:05 PDT after node removal + burst. Post-mitigation metrics attached (customer-impact-summary-20270405.pdf).
- Next 48h: Replace hardware, roll back driver to last-known-good, and patch autoscaler to reduce allocation latency for this pool class (RW-9821).
- Finance to propose credit: waive 1 day of reserved capacity charges pending PM approval — Marissa to own.
- CS to deliver executive one-pager to Sigma leadership and CISO by EOD tomorrow — Naomi to send.

Thanks to Ops and Runtime for the fast remediation. Let's ensure we capture this in the Dedicated runbook and add a play for immediate burst authorization to avoid manual exec loops next time.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Success
